demo-01: DEMO: Global mean sea level has risen by about 20 cm since 1900, and the rate of rise is accelerating.
demo-02: DEMO: Atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations have increased from about 280 ppm before the industrial era to over 410 ppm.
demo-03: DEMO: Arctic sea ice extent in September has declined by roughly 13 percent per decade since satellite records began in 1979.
demo-04: DEMO: The last decade was the warmest on record for global average surface temperature.
demo-05: DEMO: Burning fossil fuels is the main source of the increase in atmospheric CO2.
demo-06: DEMO: Most glaciers worldwide have been losing mass over recent decades.
demo-07: DEMO: Ocean acidity has increased by about 30 percent since the start of the industrial revolution as seawater absorbs CO2.
demo-08: DEMO: Solar output has shown no long-term increase since the 1950s, while global temperatures have risen.
demo-09: DEMO: Antarctica as a whole has been losing land ice, contributing to sea level rise.
demo-10: DEMO: Coral bleaching events on the Great Barrier Reef have become more frequent with marine heatwaves.
demo-11: DEMO: Methane is a greenhouse gas that is far more potent than carbon dioxide over a 20-year period.
demo-12: DEMO: Heatwaves have become more frequent and more intense across most land regions since the 1950s.
